name: Scan-to-web codes
title: Why the CueCat failed, and when scanning codes became normal
question: Why did the CueCat fail, and when did scanning real-world codes become viable?
answer: Digital:Convergence gave away millions of CueCat barcode scanners in 2000 so readers could jump from print to web pages, and shut down in 2001. Readers had to be at a computer with a cable. The idea returned once cameras were in most pockets and iOS 11 (2017) read QR codes natively in the camera app.
verdict_reason: Camera phones in three-quarters of pockets and native QR reading (2017) made scanning effortless.

constraint.name: A scanner in every pocket
constraint.detail: Scanning only works if the reader is already in your hand when you see the code.
